newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Argentina's Cavallo rules out presidential bid.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's Cavallo rules out presidential bid.

text.p: Former Argentine Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo played down talk on Tuesday of a possible presidential bid in 1999, saying he would support an ex-singer turned Peronist politician for the job.

"For the time being I have no plans to become a presidential candidate in 1999, but I do plan to support Ramon Ortega," Cavallo said, referring to a popular former singer whom he praised for his leadership as governor of Argentina's Tucuman province.

Cavallo, who spoke in an interview with the RCN radio network, was in Bogota to give a lecture to businessmen on ways of improving Colombia's financial and economic outlook. He said his own plans included a probable run for Congress next year and played down any chance of aiming for the presidency, calling Ortega a "very serious" candidate.

Cavallo, a former darling of the international financial community, faces numerous lawsuits in Buenos Aires for his charges of high-level corruption and vocal attacks on public figures, including cabinet ministers, high court justices and congressmen. He has been a thorn in the side of President Carlos Menem since he broke ranks with his government and left public office in July.
